title: The Fox's paradox
body: The author means that knowing many small things can beat knowing one big thing when the world keeps changing.
detail: In this chapter the fox stands for people who hold many loose ideas and update them; the hedgehog holds one grand theory. The author's claim is about forecasting: foxes predicted better because they changed their minds when evidence changed. That's the author's argument, not settled fact; critics note the study measured experts, not everyone. Want an example from the chapter?
